newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, recovering losses.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, recovering losses.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended higher across the board Thursday, with gold bouncing back from Wednesday's weakness, and even platinum found some support with no sign yet of Russian supplies resuming.

"Gold again ran out of sellers around $340, despite yesterday's big jump in open interest, so we saw some good shortcovering near the close," Credit Lyonnais Rouse's, chief bullion dealer in New York, Scott Mehlman, said.
"With the OTC options expiry about a week away, I don't think gold will stray too far from the $340 strike price."
COMEX August gold ended up $1.40 at $342.40 an ounce, recovering from a new contract low at $340.60 seen Wednesday on news of a proposed large increase in Belgian gold bullion coin sales from 1999.

COMEX gold open interest jumped 10,437 lots to 174,844 contracts Wednesday, as funds were seen adding to short positions to take advantage of the weak downtrend of the past few months, but some short covering was noted Thursday, traders said.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $340.20/70 an ounce, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $340.20.

On Wednesday spot gold closed around $338.90/40 in New York, not far from the four year low around $336.50 seen in February, but spot gold has found support around $340 an ounce four times since the year-to-date lows were seen.
COMEX July silver ended up 5.0 cents at $4.745 an ounce, recovering Wednesday's losses. July silver has been in a $4.65-4.90 range since mid-May.

"Much of the weakness in precious metals has been linked to the extended economic weakness in key G-7 countries and the general pursuit of strong currencies by governments and central banks, which has left investors quite willing to bear currency and inflation risk," Goldman Sachs New York-based director of commodity research, Steve Strongin said.

But "the results of the recent elections in France, which have cast doubt on the future strength of the euro, and the rather slow pace with which the Federal Reserve has responded to falling unemployment in the U.S. economy, have caused the risk to shift for the first time this decade," he said.
"Consequently there exists at least a glimmer of hope even for precious metals."
NYMEX July platinum closed up $5.80 at $412.70, its first up day in the past six trading sessions.
NYMEX July platinum open interest fell a further 705 lots to 8,910 contracts Wednesday as funds continue to liquidate and take profits on July platinum ahead of its delivery period.
July platinum open interest is equivalent to 445,500 ounces of metal, compared to NYMEX stocks of just 54,700 ounces.
NYMEX September palladium ended up 75 cents at $170.20 an ounce.

But in the physical market, the acute shortage of metal saw short term lease rates rise again Thursday, with one month platinum up to 75 pct from 50 pct Wednesday, and one month palladium up to 125 pct from 100 pct.
Russian platinum group metal (PGM) exports, suspended for five months, are due to resume in late June, with Friday June 20 often mentioned by Russian officials as a likely re-start date.
But PGM traders said Thursday that they were now hearing deliveries would not begin until some time next week, with Zurich seen a likely first delivery point, followed by Japan.
Russia supplies about 60 pct of the world's palladium and 25 pct of its platinum.
